note: One row is one rollable talent (thien phu, physicalTraitId 0..18; HV-01 and TL-01 have rollWeight 0, are form-owned exclusive characteristics and are not part of this table) running one scenario of its own mechanic family. steps is the exact call list: the Web port replays it against its own implementation and must return the same result and reach the same state after every step, not only at the end. 'a' always owns the row's talent, 't' is a talent-free dummy (TC-00, species 280). Main rows use species 280 for 'a', the one species with no design characteristic, so the row grades the talent alone; rows with combined=true put the talent on characteristic species 0 and grade the composition of both systems. Every step state additionally carries mh (maxHp), bs (base hp/attack/defense/speed) and tt (PetTraitBattleState: psa=permanentStatsApplied, phr=passiveHealRoundIndex, phc=passiveHealingCommitted, ru=reviveUses, lha=lowHpThresholdAttempted, cs=canonical [burn,corrosion,petrification,bind,paralysis] as 0/1). One op only appears here: projBeforeDamage is beforeDamage with an explicit damage kind as its last argument (projBefore is the DIRECT-only shorthand). Boundary: cs burn is 0 in every row and no row grades a burn block, because RainbowStatusCatalog registers no StatusDefinition for bank 2 / id 1 (excludedOrReserved(1) is true and BURN_RESERVED_ID has no definition), so BattleUnit.synchronizeTraitCanonicalStatuses can never set canonical BURN in production. TC-10's blocked_by [burn, corrosion] is therefore only ever blocked by corrosion, which blockedByCorrosion referees.

unitTemplate.note: Both sides are built from the traitUnit template; the actor's physicalTraitId comes from the row's traitId and the actor's speciesId from the row's speciesId. A scenario may change side, slot, stats and flags through its own steps.

randomness.note: Each scenario pins every BattleUnit random draw to the row's roll via BattleUnit.setRandomTrace under an empty context, so the engine asks with the bare label. randomLabels is the ordered list of labels the engine actually drew during the run; it is empty when a guard short-circuits before the draw. The port must ask for exactly these labels in this order and return the row's roll for each of them.
